correctness.rationale: Using Straub 2023 Theorem 1.3 (odd prime 29, Franel sporadic recurrence), the finite residue table shows exactly three zero digits d=12,14,16, with c=(7,2,5), derivative b=(3,4,18), whose unique higher-neighbor roots are 17,14,11. The d=14 root forces two zero digits and is thus excluded in the unique-zero case. Two or more zero digits force 29² divisibility. The word-count formula follows from 3*26-2=76 adjacent pairs. All 29 base residues and derivative residues are recomputed by exact recurrence and independently checked for indices 0..57 using the defining binomial sum; an additional 2600 exact index tests pass. Finite tests support but do not prove the all-index assertion.
